public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Core Automation is a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, currently targeting a Series round of $500M–$1B at a $4–5B+ valuation. The broader AI & Software sector comprises 16 identifiable peers, though the comp universe for direct valuation triangulation is constrained: one public comparable (Palantir, PLTR) and eight private peers including Palantir, Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI.

Peer-median methodology proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer coverage. A same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filter yielded fewer than three datapoints, the minimum threshold for reliable median-based analysis. The sector contains 16 peers total, but none satisfy the restrictive stage and tier criteria simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable cross-stage and cross-valuation bias given the heterogeneity of AI & Software company maturity profiles and capital requirements.

The stated valuation range of $4–5B+ reflects founder and investor expectations rather than triangulated quantitative support. Given data scarcity at the stealth stage, further valuation work would require either (1) relaxing peer filters to include adjacent-stage companies with disclosed metrics, (2) deploying revenue multiple or DCF methods if operational financials become available, or (3) awaiting market comparables from concurrent stealth-stage AI fundings. Current evidence does not support narrowing the target band below the stated $4–5B+ threshold.
